# drawbridge — search engines that are not the five herald offers
#
# Curated and pinned by SHA-256 in dist/policy.json, unlike the large upstream
# lists which rotate daily. Entries cover the parent domain only; matching is
# suffix-based, so `yandex.ru` also blocks `images.yandex.ru`.
#
# **Why this list exists.** herald offers an engine only if its safe search can
# actually be forced, and three engines were dropped on 2026-08-10 for failing
# that test. Dropping an engine from the browser's list does not make it
# unreachable: it is still a website, and typing its name into the address bar
# reaches it unfiltered. This list is the other half of that decision.
#
# What stays reachable, deliberately: DuckDuckGo, Google and Bing (all three
# rewritten to their safe hostnames by DnsFilter) and Kagi, which filters when
# logged out and offers nothing to turn that off. Nothing here may block
# `safe.duckduckgo.com`, `strict.bing.com` or `forcesafesearch.google.com` —
# those are the rewrite targets, and blocking one would take the engine down
# rather than filter it.
#
# **What this list cannot do**, stated here so nobody later mistakes it for a
# wall: the set of search engines is open. Anyone can run a SearXNG instance on
# any hostname in five minutes, and dozens of public ones exist and churn
# weekly. This blocks the engines a person can name. The backstop for the rest
# is that the adult and gambling lists block the *destinations* — an unfiltered
# engine returns a result list, and the click still fails.
# See docs/blocklist-notes.md for what was deliberately left out.

# The three herald dropped on 2026-08-10, because their safe search cannot be
# forced without TLS interception (Brave), or has no parameter to set at all
# (Startpage searches by POST), or documents one that is not heeded (Qwant).
#
# brave.com is deliberately absent: it is the vendor's site, not the engine.
# qwantjunior.com is deliberately absent: it is the filtered edition, and
# blocking a child-safe engine to enforce child safety would be perverse.
search.brave.com
startpage.com
qwant.com

# Ecosia, dropped on 2026-08-15, and the reason is the one this whole list is
# about rather than anything wrong with the engine.
#
# Its safe search is honoured, but only as a URL parameter — there is no safe
# hostname to rewrite, so the only thing that ever forced it was herald putting
# `safesearch=2` back on every load. herald is not the only browser on the
# phone: Chrome, Firefox Focus and Vivaldi are allowed too, and in any of them
# ecosia.org is unfiltered search. An engine that is safe in one of four
# browsers is a hole in the other three, and the parameter is one address-bar
# edit away even in herald.
#
# So it goes the same way Brave, Startpage and Qwant went: out of herald's
# engine list, out of `browser.search_engines`, and blocked here — because
# dropping an engine from the browser never made it unreachable. The app
# `com.ecosia.android` left `allowed_browser_packages` in the same policy and
# is blocked by name; this entry is also what stops that app working, since it
# talks to api.ecosia.org and suffix matching covers it.
ecosia.org

# Yandex, which was never offered. Each country domain is its own registrable
# name, so suffix matching does not cover them from one entry. Yandex Images is
# the specific reason this block is not optional.
yandex.com
yandex.ru
yandex.by
yandex.kz
yandex.com.tr
yandex.eu
ya.ru

# The other majors never offered. Where the parent domain is a portal carrying
# mail and other things people legitimately use, only the search host is
# blocked — the front page's search box posts to it and fails there.
baidu.com
search.yahoo.com
search.naver.com
search.daum.net
search.seznam.cz
search.aol.com
sogou.com
so.com
360.cn

# The nostalgia tier. Still live, still returning results, and still exactly as
# unforced as the day they were last fashionable.
ask.com
lycos.com
excite.com
dogpile.com
webcrawler.com
metacrawler.com
info.com
search.com

# Independent indexes. None of them filters, most of them cannot, and all of
# them are one address-bar entry away.
mojeek.com
yep.com
marginalia.nu
stract.com
rightdao.com
presearch.com
presearch.io
wiby.me
teclis.com
metager.de
swisscows.com

# Engines that market themselves on not filtering. This is the tier a teenager
# actually searches for, and the tier that rots fastest — names appear and
# disappear, so treat a miss here as expected rather than as a bug.
gibiru.com
lukol.com
freespoke.com

# Unforced front doors of the engines that ARE allowed. These resolve today and
# match none of DnsFilter's rewrite rules, so each one is the allowed engine
# without its safe hostname — which is a larger hole than any engine above.
#
# Blocking them here rather than adding them to DnsFilter is deliberate: a list
# entry reaches every phone within three hours, and a code change needs a
# release that Play Protect will not let a deployed phone install.
html.duckduckgo.com
lite.duckduckgo.com
start.duckduckgo.com
cn.bing.com
www4.bing.com
encrypted.google.com
images.google.com
